run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T02:20:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by frontend-proxy's own ingress spans carrying 503: at 02:20:47 the 1h increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 10.29 spans, all on span_name="ingress". The frontend-proxy access log gives the exact failure text: "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" with upstream cluster "frontend" and upstream host 100.70.32.128:8080 (the frontend Service ClusterIP), i.e. the frontend upstream terminated the connection before a response started; the paired "router frontend egress" spans carry error="true" with http.status_code="0". The frontend workload (frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t) is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, never restarted, records no error spans of its own and sits well under its 200Mi memory limit, but it is CPU-limited to 100m and throttled in roughly 30% of CFS periods. The 503s were already present before the chaos-mesh network-partition experiments that started at 02:18:46Z (503 logged at 02:14:08Z), and those experiments target fraud-detection and kafka pods, so they are recorded as a change during the window rather than this cause. The exact trigger inside the frontend process is unverified: frontend container logs returned no lines and the Envoy proxy configuration is not in any readable ConfigMap. A separate fraud-detection container OOMKill (exit 137, 02:20:49Z) is another workload's event and is not evidence for this alert.

claims.text: At the alert instant 02:20:47Z, the 1h increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 10.29 spans versus 34996.19 spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the error series exists only for span_name="ingress", whose 10m error increase peaked at 5.26 spans, while "router frontend egress" stayed at 0.

Sampled frontend-proxy traces between 02:05 and 02:30 contain ingress spans with status tags error=true, http.status_code="503", otel.status_code="ERROR" (4 of 5 ingress rows in the sample), for example span f82f766abfa0a3c2 in trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c, while frontend spans in the same traces show http.status_code="200".

In failing traces the frontend-proxy egress span "router frontend egress" carries error="true" and http.status_code="0" with a duration close to the failed ingress span (e.g. 799983us egress vs 800207us ingress), showing no upstream HTTP response was received on those requests.

frontend-proxy access logs record the failure exactly as "GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} ... frontend ... at 02:14:08.248Z and "GET / HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} at 02:14:08.281Z, with further identical 503 lines at 02:14:56.712Z (/api/products/1YMWWN1N4O), 02:19:24.226Z and 02:19:35.039Z (/api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N), 02:20:08.526Z (/api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N) and 02:20:36.493Z (/api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars).

Each failing request in the frontend-proxy log used a distinct ephemeral upstream source port (38158, 53652, 58238, 35714, 35938, 38664, 36714) from pod IP 100.96.4.190, while successful requests in the same window reused source port 50328; the upstream host field in those lines is the frontend Service ClusterIP 100.70.32.128:8080.

Service frontend has ClusterIP 100.70.32.128, type ClusterIP, port 8080 with a single ready endpoint frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t at 100.96.4.88:8080, so the upstream named "frontend" in the 503 lines is the frontend Deployment.

frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, container running since 2026-11-18T01:41:51Z and empty lastState; its container limit is cpu 100m / memory 200Mi (requests 50m/100Mi) with no readiness or liveness probe.

For the hour ending 02:20:47 the frontend service recorded 0 error spans on every one of its span names, including GET, POST, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, the grpc.oteldemo.* client spans, executing api route (pages) /api/* and tcp.connect.

The frontend container was CPU-throttled in 29.97%-34.19% of CFS periods across 02:00-02:35 (frontend-proxy 5.59%-7.18%), and frontend working-set memory was 123.2-128.4 MB against its 200Mi limit while frontend-proxy was about 20.2 MB against 50Mi.

frontend-proxy ingress span volume stayed at 865-967 spans per 2 minutes and the 2-minute ingress error ratio oscillated between 0 and 0.0029 from 01:58 to 02:36 (first returned sample 01:58:00 at 0.00147); at 02:20:47 the 1-minute span-based ingress error ratio was 0.00274, which does not reproduce the 0.0111 error rate in the alert annotation.

A chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition spawned NetworkChaos objects about once per minute starting 02:18:46Z; each Applied event names otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, and each experiment reached TimeUp/Recovered about 55 seconds later.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst had its container terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 02:20:49Z (restartCount 1), with kubelet Created/Started events for container fraud-detection at 02:20:49Z; its limits are cpu 100m / memory 400Mi.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo defines 12 fault-style flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) and every one has defaultVariant "off".

Other small error-span counts in the same hour ending 02:20:47 sit on flagd streaming spans - fraud-detection "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" 4.12, ad "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" 2.07 and recommendation "/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" 2.06 spans - while checkout (oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and payment spans were 0.

The frontend workload shows no crash or memory starvation: frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running/Ready, restartCount 0 with empty lastState, records 0 error spans on its own operations, and its working set stayed at 123-128 MB against a 200Mi limit.
The query of NetworkPolicy objects in namespace otel-demo returned no objects, so no NetworkPolicy in that namespace was configured to block or reset the frontend-proxy to frontend traffic.

No fault-injection setting read in otel-demo is switched on: every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap, including adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and kafkaQueueProblems, has defaultVariant "off".

The chaos-mesh network partition between fraud-detection and kafka did not cause these frontend-proxy 503s: the first 503 is logged at 02:14:08Z, before the schedule's first NetworkChaos Applied event at 02:18:46Z, and the experiments name only otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, not frontend or frontend-proxy.

Most likely mechanism, unverified on the frontend side: the frontend HTTP server closes keep-alive upstream connections and Envoy reuses such a connection at the wrong moment, which Envoy reports as upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} and returns 503 without a successful retry; consistent with every failing request using a different upstream source port while successful traffic keeps reusing source port 50328.

A contributing factor may be frontend CPU starvation: the frontend container is limited to 100m CPU and was throttled in roughly 30% of CFS periods throughout the window, which can slow request completion and widen keep-alive reuse windows; this is correlation only, not a demonstrated cause.

Align the frontend server's keep-alive and header timeouts with the frontend-proxy upstream connection pool, or add a retry policy for resets before response, so a connection-reuse race does not surface as a client-visible 503.

Review the frontend container CPU limit (100m, about 30% of CFS periods throttled) and frontend-proxy's 30m limit, and make frontend application logs plus the Envoy configuration available so the reset can be attributed inside the frontend process.

Verify the RequestErrorRate alert rule and its denominator: the rule is not loaded in this Prometheus and the annotation's 1.1% error rate is not reproducible from the span metrics (1-minute span ratio 0.27% at the alert instant).

gaps: Frontend application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs for container frontend in pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t returned 0 lines for 02:14:00-02:22:00 (that view reported status no_data, and a filtered query for 02:00-02:30 also returned nothing), so why the frontend closed upstream connections cannot be read from its own side.

The alert rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no rules from this Prometheus (both views status no_data), so the alert expression, its window and the 0.0111 denominator are unknown and the stated error rate could not be reproduced.

The frontend-proxy (Envoy) configuration governing upstream keep-alive, idle timeouts and retry policy is not in any ConfigMap readable in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist), so the connection-pool settings remain unverified.

Onset timing is only partly known: an instant query at 01:45:00Z returned no data (view status no_data), frontend-proxy logs only begin around 02:14Z, and the first returned error-metric sample is 01:58Z, so behavior before about 01:58Z is unknown.

The chaos-mesh NetworkChaos and Schedule objects themselves could not be read with the allowed Kubernetes kinds, so the experiment spec (selectors, direction, duration) is known only from event messages; whether the schedule existed before 02:18:46Z is unknown.

Why fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst was OOMKilled at 02:20:49Z and whether that relates to the fraud-detection/kafka network partition is unverified; no impact of that restart on frontend-proxy was observed.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record is available.
